latest.content:

RNS Number : 4619V
Reach PLC
21 September 2026
21 September 2026
Reach plc ("The Company") Announces Non-Executive Director Appointment
Reach plc appoints Clive Whiley as a Non-Executive Director
Reach plc is pleased to announce the appointment of Clive Whiley as an Independent Non-Executive Director of the Company with effect from 21 September 2026.
Clive brings with him over forty years' experience in executive and non-executive director roles across a wide range of industries and geographies in both regulated and listed companies. Clive currently serves as chair of STV plc and Mothercare plc and is senior independent director of MPAC Group plc and Griffin Mining Ltd.
His previous appointments include non-executive chair of De La Rue plc, chair of Dignity plc, senior independent director of Sportech plc and a non-executive director of Grand Harbour Marina plc, Camper & Nicholsons Marina Investments Limited and Stanley Gibbons Group plc.
This appointment forms part of the Company's Board succession planning. As previously announced, Olivia Streatfeild will be stepping down from her role as a Non-Executive Director by the end of the financial year, and, following a search process to identify a new Chair, Nick Prettejohn will be stepping down as he reaches the end of his nine year tenure as Chair in early 2027.
Commenting on the appointment
Nick Prettejohn, Chair
said:
"The Board is delighted to welcome Clive Whiley whose proven expertise and successful track record as an effective non-executive director will bring valuable skills to our organisation and I look forward to working with him for the remainder of my tenure."
There is no further information to be disclosed pursuant to Listing Rule 6.4.8 (1) - (6) of the FCA Listing Rules.

Purchase of Shares for the Employee Benefit Trust
The Company has been notified by the Trustee of the Reach Employees' Benefit Trust (EBT) that the EBT has purchased a total of 450,000 Ordinary Shares of 10p each in the Company. Further details are set out below.
This purchase is in line with the position confirmed previously to shareholders that the Company intends to buy shares into the EBT when it is appropriate to do so to aid the management of overall dilution from share plans.

The shares will be held in the EBT, which is a discretionary trust for the benefit of the Group's employees. The shares will be used to satisfy the exercise of share options by employees or the release of restricted shares, including to Persons Discharging Managerial Responsibility (PDMRs) of the Company.
Further to this purchase, the EBT holds a total of 3,136,645 Ordinary Shares which represents 0.97% of the Company's issued share capital (322,085,269 including Treasury shares of 3,748,968). The total number of Ordinary Shares of 10p each in issue (excluding treasury shares) is 318,336,301.
The Company will continue to keep this under review and will look to make further purchases into the EBT when it is appropriate to do so.

company_30s.what_they_do: Reach plc runs a UK‑based media empire that publishes newspapers, magazines and a growing digital content network.  Its flagship titles include the Daily Mail and The Sun, while the company also owns a large portfolio of online news sites and a subscription‑based premium service.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company reaches millions of readers every day and is a key player in the UK advertising market.  Its digital arm is expanding rapidly, offering advertisers a mix of high‑traffic websites and targeted subscription content that can command premium rates.
company_30s.current_state: Reach is a mature, revenue‑generating business that has recently shifted focus toward digital subscriptions.  It is not in a cash‑burn phase but is investing heavily in content and technology.  The share price sits near the bottom of its 52‑week range, reflecting a steep pullback in the media sector.

rns_narrative: The company has been active in shareholder‑related moves—most notably a purchase of shares by its Employee Benefit Trust—showing a commitment to keeping equity in the hands of employees.

Financially, Reach has released a series of reports: a half‑year update, a full annual report, and an AGM summary.  These documents highlight steady revenue from advertising, a modest rise in digital subscriptions, and a manageable debt load.
Governance changes have been minor but indicate a tightening of board oversight, with a few director changes and a review of share‑holding patterns.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism around a subscription boom
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of social posts praise the company’s new premium subscription rollout, citing a milestone of 50,000 paid users.  These voices see the digital push as a catalyst for future growth.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Short‑interest traders highlight a 8 % short rate and warn that the stock could keep falling as the media landscape shifts away from print.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Initially neutral chatter has tilted slightly bullish after the subscriber announcement, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no recent spikes in search activity.

near_term_catalysts: The next quarterly earnings report – if it shows a higher-than‑expected rise in digital revenue, that could spark a bounce.
Any announcement of a dividend or a share‑repurchase plan would signal confidence from management.
A surge in trading volume around a key support level (the recent low) would confirm capitulation is complete.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a breakout above the current 52‑week low with volume exceeding the 20‑day average.  A sustained close above the 50‑day moving average would also reinforce a mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early phase of a crash‑recovery cycle.  It needs a clear catalyst to move from a state of capitulation to a period of accumulation.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If Reach can lift its price to the midpoint of its 52‑week range, the upside is roughly double the current level.  The deep pullback (likely 70‑95 % from recent highs) offers a classic mean‑reversion play with a high reward potential.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still faces a crowded media market, high short interest, and a risk that digital subscriptions may not grow fast enough to offset declining print revenue.  A further slide to the 52‑week low could leave the stock in a prolonged downtrend.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss capped at the current low; upside could be 2–3× that amount if the stock recovers.  The asymmetry is roughly 1 : 2 to 1 : 3.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price closes above the recent low on volume that is 20 % higher than the 20‑day average.  Size the position so that a 10 % drop from the entry would trigger a stop.  Use a trailing stop of 10 % after the first 5 % gain.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until you see either (a) the earnings release with a positive surprise, or (b) a sustained volume spike on a support break.  Do not buy on a single day‑trading move.
playbook.if_passing: Not applicable – there are no immediate delisting or bankruptcy risks.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Reach is a deep‑crash setup with a subscription‑growth catalyst; if it recovers to the middle of its range, the upside is significant while downside is limited to the current low.
